_comment: Per-company compensation structure facts for the scorer (Module 3). The purpose is COMPENSATION NORMALIZATION: postings from Google, Meta, and similar companies list BASE SALARY only, then '+ bonus + equity'. Reading a posted base range as total comp UNDERSTATES a role and wrongly dings seniority/level fit. These facts let the scorer normalize a posted base range to an APPROXIMATE total-comp figure before grading Sam's seniority/level-up bar (~L6 AWS Sr Manager TOTAL comp, not base). Numbers here are considered grounded (locked) — do not edit casually; SAM's bar is in profile.json / locked_facts. Non-listed companies fall back to the 'default' entry.

sam_bar.label: Sam's level bar is TOTAL compensation, not base
sam_bar.bar_is: total comp including equity, not base salary
sam_bar.note: Grade seniority_fit and the level-up rule against LEVEL + NORMALIZED TOTAL COMP, never the raw posted base number.

Google.normalize_hint: A Google base range ≈ 60% of total comp → approximate TC ≈ base / 0.60. A posted level chip ('Mid' vs 'Advanced') is authoritative for level.

Google DeepMind.normalize_hint: Same Google comp structure (DeepMind roles post on Google's comp schedule).

Meta.normalize_hint: Base is a minority of total comp; approximate TC ≈ base / 0.55-0.60.

Amazon.normalize_hint: Amazon TC is dominated by back-loaded RSUs + sign-on; a posted base vastly understates TC, and base caps do NOT indicate a level cap. Internal-transfer roles skew to total-target (see internal-transfer context).

OpenAI.normalize_hint: OpenAI posts salary ranges that are usually base; add bonus + equity context.

Anthropic.normalize_hint: Anthropic ranges are base; total comp is meaningfully higher.

NVIDIA.normalize_hint: NVIDIA's total comp is well above base.

Snowflake.normalize_hint: Base is only part of Snowflake TC.

Databricks.normalize_hint: Databricks TC is base + bonus + equity.

CoreWeave.normalize_hint: Treat posted base as base, not total.

default.posted_range_is: base unless explicitly labeled 'total compensation', 'OTE', or 'total comp'
default.normalize_hint: When a posting lists only ONE range plus '+ bonus + equity' or similar, assume it is BASE salary and do NOT read it as total comp. Do not penalize a role just because bonus/equity are not included in the posted base range. If the range is explicitly labeled total/OTE, treat it as total.
